title: phases-file tier ingestion, and the two further breaks between a planner's intent and a dispatched model (gh-434)
body:
Closes #434.

`fr plan create --phases-file` silently dropped `phase.tier`. This wires it end
to end — and, in the process, found that #434 was one of **three** breaks
between a planner's intent and a dispatched subagent's model.

- **Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-20-phases-file-tier-reaches-dispatch-design.md`
- **Plan:** `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-20-phases-file-tier-reaches-dispatch/` (5 phases, all complete)

## The bug, reproduced on this PR's own plan

The plan implementing this fix was scaffolded by the command it fixes. Its
phases file declared a tier on all five phases. What landed:

```
01.yaml: 0 tier key(s), 1 skeleton, 1 acceptance
02.yaml: 0 tier key(s), 0 skeleton, 1 acceptance
…  exit 0, no warning
```

`skeleton` and `acceptance` survived; `tier` did not. The tiers were restored by
hand — the exact workaround #434 reports being applied three times in another
repo — and journaled as evidence rather than quietly worked around.

## Three breaks, all closed

| # | Break | Closed by |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `--phases-file` dropped `tier` (`plan_cmd.py`, `plan_ops.py`) | phase 1 |
| 2 | No skill told a planner to write one — `fr-plan/SKILL.md` never said the word, while fr-goal §3 asserted "fr-plan tags each phase a `tier`" | phase 5 T1 |
| 3 | `fr` never resolved the `from_phase` sentinel — the dispatch brief handed the orchestrator the literal string | phases 3 + 5 T3 |

Break 3 was found while checking whether the operator's chosen test was even
writable. It was not: `_build_member_brief` returned the manifest literal, so
the join from sentinel to concrete tier was LLM prose.

## On the #498 question — the premise, corrected

The goal asked whether #434 explains most of #498, on the premise that `tier`
"never reaches the plan on any harness at all". **It does not, and the
correction is the more useful finding.**

`tier` *does* reach this repo's plans — `2026-09-19-opencode-subagent-dispatch`
and `2026-09-20-opencode-tier-binding-reaches-dispatch` both carry real tiers.
They got there by **hand-edit**, proven by key order: `_build_phase_doc` appends
`acceptance`/`skeleton` at the *end* of the header, but in both plans `tier`
sits between `tag` and `depends_on`, which the emitter cannot produce.

So #498's break was independent and #504 fixed it correctly. What #434
contributes is narrower but still live: tier arrival depended on a planning
agent inserting a key **no skill instructed and no CLI accepted** — and
post-#504 that is *more* dangerous, not less, because the agent files now carry
correct models, so an untiered dispatch is indistinguishable from working
tiering.

## Live evidence — the fix drove the pipeline that built it

Early in the run, this branch's own cursor emitted:

```json
{"item": "phase/1", "tier": "from_phase"}
```

After phase 3 landed, the same command on the same run emitted:

```json
{"item": "phase/4", "tier": "from_phase", "resolved_tier": "hard"}
```

`hard` then resolved to `claude-opus-5` and dispatched phase 4 — the phase that
proves the chain — on it. Both observations are in one transcript.

## What changed

- **`PhaseSpec.tier`** + emission (omitted when unset, byte-stable) + ingestion.
  An invalid tier is refused in `create()`'s **pre-flight** loop, not at the
  post-write re-parse that strands a half-built folder (#133).
- **`fr plan self-review`** gains an `fr_version` floor probe for `tier`
  (3.12.0) and a warning for an untiered agentic phase. Both `warn` — no exit
  code moves. All three floor probes now share one helper.
- **`resolved_tier`** on the member dispatch brief. `tier` keeps its meaning as
  the manifest's faithful echo; the group brief deliberately has no such key.
- **`fr-plan`** instructs the tier; **`fr-goal` §5** reads `resolved_tier`.
- Matrix corrected; **4.8.0 → 4.8.1** (patch).

## Findings, fixed

Six, every one found by the per-phase review rather than by CI. Full text:
`fr journal render --scope plan --slug 2026-09-20-phases-file-tier-reaches-dispatch --section findings`

| id | finding |
|---|---|
| `p1-f1` | Byte-stability — an explicit spec goal — had **no test at all**. Fixed class-wide; mutation-verified that emitting `tier` unconditionally now fails. |
| `p1-f2` | The derived test gave phase 1 `depends_on: [1]`, a self-dependency that would break confusingly once `_preflight_phase_error` grows a cycle check. |
| `p2-f1-shared-fixture` | The untiered warning broke 3 unrelated `self_review(...) == []` tests via the shared `v2_plan_minimal` fixture. Fixed the way the skeleton gate fixed the same fixture in `c46cebe`. |
| `p2-f2` | Two of three floor probes extracted, leaving the third **claiming to be the same** in its own comment. Routed through the helper; all 11 skeleton-gate tests pass unchanged. |
| `p3-f1` | `resolved_tier` shipped but no skill named it — mechanism closed, instruction not. Scheduled as a new task rather than widening phase 3; resolved by P5.T3. |
| `p5-f1` | AGENTS.md documents one generated mirror; **CI enforces two**. The missing `.hermes/` entry is what produced an unexplained "fourth" test failure. |

## Decisions

`fr journal render --scope plan --slug 2026-09-20-phases-file-tier-reaches-dispatch --section decisions`;
the five operator-answered ones are in the spec's Decisions section (D1–D5),
each recording the question put and the option chosen.

## Operator gates

```
brainstorm: operator gate answered by the operator
```

One batched Q&A (4 questions), plus one follow-up when a discovery invalidated
the premise of an answer — `from_phase` being unresolved meant the chosen test
was not writable as specified. D5 is that follow-up's answer.

## Acceptance

`fr acceptance check` → `127 rows OK ({'ci': 105, 'skipped': 18, 'not-implemented': 4})`

**Rows added since `origin/main`** (`fr acceptance check --added-since origin/main`), each defended:

- `phase-header-fields-survive-phases-file` — the *class* claim behind #434. The
  ingestion whitelist will drift again at the next added field; the test is
  derived from `PhaseHeader.model_fields`, so it covers that field without an edit.
- `phase-tier-reaches-the-dispatch-brief` — the join. Every link had unit
  coverage while the chain was broken; this is the row that says the chain works.
- `plan-self-review-flags-tier-gaps` — makes the untiered case observable at plan
  time. Business-level because it changes what an operator is told, not how.

**Corrected overclaim:** `fr-goal-phase-tiering` sat at `ci` claiming "fr-plan
annotates each phase with a tier; the orchestrator dispatches that phase's
subagent at the mapped model", while its levels pinned `PhaseHeader.tier` and
`fr models resolve` **in isolation** — nothing pinned that a planner's tier
reaches a plan, and until this PR it could not. Notes now say so, and say what
is still *not* claimed.

**Pre-existing debt** (18 `skipped`, 4 `not-implemented`) is unchanged by this PR.

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest` (full, coverage) | 3304 passed, 80 skipped, **3 failed** (see below); coverage **91.72%** vs 75% floor |
| `ruff check` / `format` | clean |
| `mypy` (4 src trees) | no issues, 138 files |
| `fr acceptance check` | 127 rows OK |
| `fr validate artifacts` | 33 artifacts, all valid |
| `fr journal check --scope plan` | clean |
| `fr harness parity --check` | agrees |
| `fr plan self-review` | passed |
| `sync-opencode --check` / `bump-version --check` | in sync / versions agree |

**The 3 local failures are pre-existing and environment-dependent, not from this
PR.** Independently confirmed by reverting this branch's source and watching them
fail identically, and `main`'s CI is green at `eb85d91`. One is worth a separate
issue: `test_cli_all_fails_when_nothing_is_discoverable` fails *because* super-fr
is marketplace-installed locally, so the shipped manifest stays discoverable
after the test defeats the wheel copy — the test's own docstring is about that
leak class, inverted. **CI, not my machine, is the arbiter here.**

## Test Plan — post-merge, operator-driven

Items 1–5 are automated and green in CI. Item 6 verbatim from the spec:

> 6. **Post-merge, operator-driven — not claimed by CI**: no automated level
>    dispatches a real subagent and reads back the session row's model. That live
>    claim remains with `opencode-subagent-dispatch` at `skipped`, whose scope
>    correction already records why.

No manual phases in this plan; nothing ships unimplemented.
